5. On receipt of the said petition for cancellation of the order the Assistant Judge without considering the grounds of objection raised by the defendants rejected the petition of suit. On 28.5.90 the defendants also closed their evidence but the Assistant Judge after closing of evidence of both parties fixed 6.6.90 as the date for examination of the afore-mentioned three persons as court witnesses. The defendants apprehended that they may not get fair justice from the court of the Assistant Judge filed Misc. Case under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned District Judge, Faridpur being Misc. Case No. 18 of 1990. The said Misc. Case is pending disposal. 

 7. Mr. Md. Nurul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned Assistant Judge's order of summoning the aforesaid witnesses as court witnesses is not warranted by law as this Rule 14 of Order 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submits that the Court cannot examine anybody on the application of any of the parties as court witnesses. In the instant case the learned Assistant Judge issued the summons to the witnesses not on his own motion but on the desire and application of the plaintiff. He further submits that the witnesses namely, Niranjan Majumder was not a stranger to the suit but he was a party as defendant to the suit namely defendant No. 7. In order to consider the submission made by the learned lawyer for the petitioner the provision of Order 16 Rule 14 need to be looked into which provides for the court to summon as witnesses strangers to suit. Order 16 Rule 14 C.P.C. reads as follows: - 

 9. Mr. Md. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 has drawn my attention to Order 16 Rule 2 which provides that a party applying for summons shall, before the summons is granted and within a period to be fixed, pay into court such a sum of money as appears to the court be sufficient to defray the travelling and other expenses of person summoned in passing to and from the Court in which he is required to attend, and for one day's attendance. This Rule 2 of order 16 merely provides for the procedure and the requirement to make payment for summoning his witness and does not provide for any party to apply for summoning a person who is not a party as court witness. In the instant case there was an application by a party to summon certain persons as court witnesses for which the court's power and the procedure has been made in Order XVI Rule 14 quoted above.
